title: Exact integer generation, seed initialization and state restoration in Rand32 and Rand64
explanation: For oorandom 11.1.5, twelve unchanged APIs have exact value/state proofs: new, new_inc, state, from_state, the unsigned output method and the signed output method for both Rand32 and Rand64. For arbitrary seed and increment input, new_inc normalizes the stream to ((increment << 1) OR 1), starts at zero, performs one PCG state update, adds the seed modulo the state width, then performs a second PCG state update. new uses the published DEFAULT_INC. state returns the exact current state and increment, and from_state restores those values unchanged; two additional composition theorems establish save/restore identity. Unsigned generation returns the exact PCG-XSH-RR output permutation of the old state and advances to multiplier*state+increment modulo 2^64 or 2^128. Signed generation preserves that updated state and reinterprets the unsigned result bits as i32 or i64. Each covered call terminates normally in the Aeneas model for every scalar input, including zero states and even restored increments. Separate Kani harnesses directly check both original rand_float methods after restoring arbitrary complete state and increment, including zero states and even increments. Each returns an IEEE value greater than or equal to zero and strictly less than one (two harnesses, 33 checks each). This is a separate range-only body guarantee; exact float bits and poststate were not established, and no cross-tool equivalence or Aeneas machine claim is added.
trusted_assumptions: The Rust compiler, official Charon/Aeneas translation, official Aeneas scalar models and Lean kernel are trusted. No custom external models or local trusted helper contracts are used. All fourteen public and supplementary theorem dependency audits permit only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. Standard-library wrapping, casts, shifts and rotations use official Aeneas models, rather than body proofs of Rust std implementations.
environment: Original crates.io oorandom 11.1.5 src/Cargo.toml, archive-compared without changes. Rust nightly-2026-09-17; Charon 08d7c9d50144bd84848212c24701253585e90d1f; official Aeneas frontend/library be86ab0f1989d04944292b345b24c435be3ad10a; Lean 4.35.0. Official targeted extraction selects all twelve original bodies and their shared callees. Original tests, regeneration hashes and integrated Lean/axiom audits are retained in evidence.
limitations: The proof covers twelve integer/state APIs on x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu with the original default configuration. Exact rand_float output bits/poststate and rand_range for both generators remain unproved; separate Kani evidence establishes only the rand_float output range, as do non-excluded inherited/default and external blanket methods. The save/restore composition theorem establishes pure state identity; no arbitrary user callback or destructor behavior is modeled. No period, statistical distribution, independence or cryptographic guarantee is established. Other targets were not checked.
tool_limitations: Lean backend only, requiring cargo-proofs 0.4.0 or later. The version identifies the official Aeneas Git revision pinned in lake-manifest.json (backends/lean); this revision uses Lean 4.35.0. The recorder checks committed Lean theorem declarations and permits only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound as transitive axioms. It rejects sorryAx and custom axioms, including axiomatized external models. Charon/Aeneas extraction is not rerun. The author must review that the committed functional model matches the recorded Rust source, that the named theorem corresponds to the public API, and that the reported precondition matches the theorem. A checked theorem alone does not establish those links or the adequacy of the specification. The current adapter records the default Cargo configuration, with ordinary Lean module paths and a pinned official Git dependency. Other backends, custom Lake source directories, and local-path Aeneas dependencies are unsupported. See https://proofs.rs/book/aeneas.html and https://github.com/AeneasVerif/aeneas/tree/be86ab0f1989d04944292b345b24c435be3ad10a.

Unsigned generation returns the exact PCG-XSH-RR output permutation of the old state and advances to multiplier*state+increment modulo 2^64 or 2^128. Signed generation preserves that updated state and reinterprets the unsigned result bits as i32 or i64. Each covered call terminates normally in the Aeneas model for every scalar input, including zero states and even restored increments. Separate Kani harnesses directly check both original rand_float methods after restoring arbitrary complete state and increment, including zero states and even increments. Each returns an IEEE value greater than or equal to zero and strictly less than one (two harnesses, 33 checks each). This is a separate range-only body guarantee; exact float bits and poststate were not established, and no cross-tool equivalence or Aeneas machine claim is added.
claims.shared_trusted_assumptions: The Rust compiler, official Charon/Aeneas translation, official Aeneas scalar models and Lean kernel are trusted. No custom external models or local trusted helper contracts are used. All fourteen public and supplementary theorem dependency audits permit only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. Standard-library wrapping, casts, shifts and rotations use official Aeneas models, rather than body proofs of Rust std implementations.
claims.shared_limitations: The proof covers twelve integer/state APIs on x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu with the original default configuration. Exact rand_float output bits/poststate and rand_range for both generators remain unproved; separate Kani evidence establishes only the rand_float output range, as do non-excluded inherited/default and external blanket methods. The save/restore composition theorem establishes pure state identity; no arbitrary user callback or destructor behavior is modeled. No period, statistical distribution, independence or cryptographic guarantee is established. Other targets were not checked.
